evidence.source: Shuowen.org, 《說文解字》 entry with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry gives the gloss ‘a room beside [the main room]’ and analyzes 房 as 从戶方聲. Duan Yucai explains the main room and rooms on its left and right, and mentions an extended use for a compartment of a ritual vessel. This is a received lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the graph’s first formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「房」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.field: recorded form categories and component roles
evidence.text: The page labels the displayed form categories 楚系簡帛文字, 小篆, and 說文; it identifies 戶 as the semantic element and 方 as the phonetic element. Its text confirms these categories and roles, but the page’s glyphs were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢字「房」：字形演變

evidence.field: reported earliest graphic attestation and graphic development
evidence.text: The inspected page states that 房 first appears in Warring States writing and that forms from Warring States through seal, clerical, and regular scripts retain 戶 plus phonetic 方. It says some Chu-slip forms add a short stroke above 戶. Its further proposal that 方 contributes ‘side’ is secondary speculation, not established by the Shuowen graph analysis. No manuscript image was visually inspected for this report.
evidence.title: 房字形演变字源_汉字「房」

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 房 entry, historical phonology table
evidence.field: phonetic component and character historical pronunciation
evidence.text: The page reports 房 with Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[Cə-N-]paŋ and Zhengzhang *baŋ, alongside 方 as the phonetic. In the Zhengzhang phonetic-series list, 房 is *baːŋ/*baŋ and 方 is *paŋ/*baŋ; the 房 entry’s Middle Chinese table includes bjang and bang for distinct readings. These reconstructions and transcriptions are system-specific comparisons, not direct recordings of Old Chinese. Their approximate correspondence supports a phonetic role for 方. It does not establish 方’s possible extra semantic contribution ‘side’.
evidence.title: 房 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 房 entry, Mandarin and Cantonese reading data
evidence.text: The entry reports Mandarin fáng and Cantonese Jyutping pong4 for the displayed standard/Guangzhou-Hong Kong scope. The local dossier separately records Cantonese fong4; this difference in the supplied readings was not resolved against an authoritative Cantonese dictionary in this search.
evidence.title: 房 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Revised Mandarin Dictionary
evidence.field: modern senses and cited literary examples
evidence.text: The dictionary lists ‘dwelling/house’, an individual room, structures resembling a room, family branches, wife/concubine senses, and several classifier uses. It cites Cao Pi’s Three Kingdoms-era 燕歌行 with 空房, among other examples. The cited periods document uses, but the dictionary’s ordering does not establish a complete chronological chain of semantic change.
evidence.title: 《重編國語辭典修訂本》房

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Excavated Documents and Paleography, Li Shoukui, discussion of Baoshan Chu slips
evidence.text: The article identifies the 房 graph on Baoshan slip 149 as an example of the Chu form of 戶, and says the short top horizontal stroke can be an optional decorative mark. This supports a local graphic variation in the 戶 element; it does not itself date the earliest use of the 房 graph or establish a semantic extension.
evidence.title: 李守奎：包山楚簡120——123號簡補釋

evidence.field: seal-script glyph candidate provenance and rights
evidence.text: The file page describes 房-seal.svg as a Shuowen seal-script-style vector redraw, attributes the digital file to the listed contributor, and states that it is a public-domain picture of an ancient script. It is a modern digital representation, not an artifact photograph. The file page links the Sinica Database and other source databases as available sources.
evidence.title: File:房-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Chinese Character Database rights notice
evidence.text: The official notice URL was opened but returned no readable page text in the web result. The character database page itself states ‘All Rights Reserved’; this notice was therefore not used to establish reuse rights for its glyph image.
evidence.title: 智財權聲明

search_audit.outcome: Opened the character database rights URL and Xiaoxuetang homepage URL, but neither returned readable notice text in the tool output. The character entry itself labels historical forms, but its glyph assets were not selected because reuse permission was not verified.

gaps: No image pixels were visually inspected. The selected Commons file is explicitly a modern digital vector redraw in a Shuowen seal-script style, not an ancient artifact photograph.

The Warring States first-graphic-attestation statement is reported by the opened Guoxuedashi page, but no primary manuscript publication or excavated object image was directly inspected here. The report should be treated as a cautious attestation boundary, not proof that the spoken word or graph did not exist earlier.

No securely dated early textual context establishing the precise earliest sense was inspected. Shuowen gives a side-room gloss; the MOE dictionary’s later cited examples support later house, room, and other senses, but their dictionary sequence does not independently prove semantic chronology.
No graph corruption or reanalysis event is established by the inspected sources. The optional short horizontal mark in some Chu forms is described as decoration, not corruption.

方’s proposed extra semantic contribution ‘side’ remains uncertain; sound correspondences support its phonetic role. 戶 is the conventional semantic element, associated with doors/household structures in the compound analysis.
The local dossier’s reported Sino-Tibetan comparisons were not independently investigated in this search. They should remain speculative, not established etymology.
The CText early-poem result and its competing interpretations of 由房 were not revisited; the precise early phrase sense remains open.

No direct source page for the alleged earliest sound/name behind a whole-graph loan was identified. The conventional analysis treats 房 as a phonosemantic compound, and no whole-graph loan claim is supported here.
Cantonese reading data vary between the local dossier’s fong4 and Wiktionary’s pong4 for its stated Guangzhou/Hong Kong scope; an authoritative dialect dictionary check is still needed.
The Academia Sinica character-form page was used as linked evidence only. Its rights-notice page did not yield readable text, so no Academia Sinica image was proposed.
